notes: The fix is sound: WBL replay records which segment last references each duplicate ref, the checkpoint keeps those series records, and `truncateOOO` releases them once the WBL is truncated past that segment. The added test reproduces the issue's sequence and checks restart after OOO compaction and expiry cleanup, though the failing package suite (cause unknown, possibly a flake) and refs lingering if OOO compaction never runs cost some confidence.

The fix targets the root cause: during WBL replay it records duplicate refs (samples, histograms, float histograms and mmap markers) against the WBL segment that uses them. The checkpoint then keeps those series records, and they are released once OOO compaction truncates the WBL past that segment. This covers both the restart-survival requirement and the no-retention-forever requirement, and the end-to-end and unit tests are solid. However, the tsdb package suite failed, possibly from an existing test that expects duplicate series records to expire by timestamp alone, so a regression cannot be ruled out.

Adds an exact `hreflect.CompareNumbers` that handles the trunc/fraction, overflow-bound, NaN and Inf cases, and uses it in `Eq`, `compareGet` and `where`'s `checkCondition`; this fixes the int/float mismatch, the old negative-int-to-uint64 overflow and the unset uint64-left bug, with thorough unit, where and integration tests.

Adds an exact helper, hreflect.CompareNumbers, that compares every mix of signed, unsigned and float values by trunc-then-compare, handling NaN, ±Inf, out-of-range floats and negative-vs-uint, and wires it into Eq, compareGetWithCollator and Where's checkCondition (removing the now-dead compareTwoUints), so all six functions agree and the issue's precision and overflow cases are covered by unit, Where and integration tests; the only nit is that Where's numeric fast path duplicates the operator switch.

Merging by chunk disk-ref order keeps the live series' newer in-order and OOO mapped chunks, fixing the reported loss and the duplicate-chunk problem; but when the duplicate ref has no mapped chunks it keeps every attached chunk, so already-compacted history can come back (likely related to the failed package suite), and the WAL-corruption case is not tested, though the new test covers all sample types and replays twice.

The patch passes the hidden PR test but the package suite fails, and its fix rests on a fragile heuristic: on a duplicate ref it keeps chunks whose disk ref is newer than the duplicate's last chunk, and keeps everything when the duplicate has no chunks. That fallback can retain already-compacted OOO history the issue says should be cleaned up, and the WAL-corruption case is untested; the new test is thorough across sample types with a double replay.

The design is sound and follows the spec: an appending option parser, names added to the automate loader even with auto_https off, a skip when a site policy already covers the name, an explicit internal-issuer split for non-public names, and global-option fill-in via the existing policy path. However, it builds a separate parallel policy path instead of reusing the site-block flow, its adapt output evidently diverges from the expected JSON (hidden test 0/1), and it adds subjects-only policies that may not match site-block output in every scenario.

The design is sound: names are appended to the automate loader even with auto_https off, policies come from newBaseAutomationPolicy so global options apply, non-public names get an explicit internal issuer, and names already covered by a site-block policy are skipped; it still fails the hidden adapt test, most likely an exact-output difference (policy or subject ordering) I could not pin down, and the helper takes warnings by value so any warnings it adds are lost.
